source.stem:
A student wishes to find the volume of a small, irregularly-shaped stone.
A ruler and a measuring cylinder containing some water are available.
Which apparatus is needed?

options.text: neither the ruler nor the measuring cylinder
the ruler and the measuring cylinder

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: Store the pair with unlike poles on the same side, wood between them, and hard steel pieces across the ends.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: Store the pair touching directly, with unlike poles on the same side and soft iron across the ends; no wood is needed.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: Keep magnets away from every metal object, including soft iron storage pieces.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: Put soft rubber pieces across the ends of the stored magnets.

intelligence.enrichment: Magnets should not be heated, dropped, hammered, or kept near mobile phones or remote controls. They should be stored in pairs with unlike poles on the same side, a piece of wood between them, and soft iron pieces across the ends. handling and storage choices determine whether magnets are treated safely The learner chooses safe handling and storage: no heating, dropping, hammering, or placement near mobile phones or remote controls, and storage in pairs with unlike poles, wood, and soft iron pieces. Magnets are hard objects, so heating, hammering, or keeping them near devices should not matter.
